title: Execution targets and rebind
summary: Frozen targets and digests stay as provenance across authorized takeover and never gate a write. Current execution ownership, same-target ancestry, tenant/project/member or shared-group authority and endpoint checks remain required. QA tests whatever is deployed: QA start reports a different served commit and proceeds, and every deployment-bound browser case records the commit its environment served at case start. Once the successor has a ready deploy receipt, execution and mission views name its pinned release_version, and command cases check out the current owning run's project source. A takeover tells each moved member owner once that QA moved to the successor and opens at its item QA stage; the predecessor wake is not the command. An owner whose carried walk is still open under a live session gets no takeover notice and no successor stage wake: the walk keeps going and may pass on the newer build. An inherited fail whose latest failing attempt was created before this run, and whose merge is in the current release, retries with yoke qa plan run --item REF --stage STAGE --project SLUG. A failure created after this run gets the ordinary rework handoff. Materialization rebinds open private and run QA requirements in place to the successor receipt, keeping each case ID and prior target JSON. A predecessor pass carries only across the same destination, including repeated takeovers; otherwise the case is owed again. Shared plan groups retain their own group identities and frozen targets. Begun executions and captures keep their frozen targets; an execution that has run, leased and recorded nothing, such as one waiting for its Test Machine turn, takes the successor's current roster and target when its owner begins it again, keeping its execution ID, execution_order and host-line place. Neither observation changes nor early verdicts grant release approval. Manual-only takeover notices tell holders without a future scheduled wake to check the evidence and schedule their next recheck before parking; no dispatch wakes them for it. Steering recipients must staff the item for that check. Holders with future scheduled rechecks receive no manual-only takeover notice; automatic or mixed requirements keep successor dispatch guidance.
